_README: Frames captured verbatim from the vendor app, used to prove the builders in
zengge/protocol.py reproduce real traffic byte for byte.
1. A golden frame is EVIDENCE, not an expected value. If a test fails,
the builder is wrong. NEVER edit capture_hex to make a test pass.
2. Captures must be NEUTRAL. Create a throwaway schedule/scene in the app
purely to capture it -- do not paste in your own saved scenes, palettes
or schedule times. This repository is public and those are personal.
3. Capture against tools/fakedevice.py, not real hardware. Timer slots are
capture_hex is the frame EXACTLY as it appeared on the wire, including the
b0 b1 b2 b3 wrapper if one was present. The test unwraps it before comparing,
so the wrapper's per-message counter does not matter.
Set framing to what you actually observed: 'wrapped' if the bytes begin
b0 b1 b2 b3, otherwise 'bare'. This field is itself under test.
Entries whose capture_hex is 'TODO' are skipped.

captures.name: timer_write_power_on
captures.note: PRIORITY. Settles whether an e0 05 message is bare or wrapped, and whether its inner checksum survives inside a wrapper. Create a throwaway timer at a neutral time -- 07:00, every day, action 'turn on'.

captures.name: timer_delete
captures.note: Delete the throwaway timer above and capture the command.

captures.name: timer_write_disabled
captures.note: Same timer, toggled OFF in the app. Confirms the enabled flag is the only byte that changes.

captures.name: scene_three_primaries
captures.note: Build a NEW scene in the app with exactly three entries -- pure red, pure green, pure blue -- at speed 50, brightness 100. Neutral by construction. Settles e1 21 header byte 7 and the 5th colour-entry byte.

captures.name: per_pixel_small
captures.note: PRIORITY. A doodle on a SHORT run if you can configure one, else note the real N here and use neutral colours. Settles whether the 7th entry byte is a white channel or a per-entry brightness -- send one fully saturated colour and read that byte.

args.colors: TODO: one entry per light, in strand order

captures.name: solid_color_warm_white
captures.note: Pick any colour in the app's colour wheel and capture. Confirms the e0 01 00 a1 layout and the 0x14 constant.

captures.name: power_on
captures.note: Tap the power toggle on. Confirms bare framing for 71 23 0f.

captures.name: state_reply
captures.note: A real 28-byte EA 81 reply, parsed rather than built. Any state is fine; it reveals no personal detail beyond which scene was active, so capture one with the lights on a plain colour.
